headline: High-risk pair: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API surfaces, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop ingests uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and app content by default, so malicious content can be treated as instructions. OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces, creating a plausible bridge if its outputs are fed into ChatGPT. The pairwise interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is copied into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard or file upload, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF OpenMetadata outputs are routed through MCP or webhooks into ChatGPT Desktop, attacker-controlled text can influence instructions.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools.
Require a human review step before pasting OpenMetadata output into ChatGPT.
Strip instructions from any OpenMetadata-exported text before upload.
Use separate workspaces for raw catalog data and ChatGPT prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to OpenMetadata outputs before they reach ChatGPT.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and supported-app content, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge metadata through APIs and MCP. If sensitive catalog data is moved into ChatGPT, it can be exposed to vendor-mediated inference; the reverse path is less direct but still plausible through shared workflows. This is a documented-surface inference, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF sensitive lineage or governance exports are uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop, they enter vendor-mediated processing.
IF OpenMetadata data is copied into ChatGPT via screenshots or files, the same data class can appear in ChatGPT outputs.
mitigations: Avoid uploading catalog exports containing sensitive metadata.
Redact identifiers before moving OpenMetadata content into ChatGPT.
Use a separate non-sensitive sample dataset for ChatGPT analysis.
Limit ChatGPT sessions to synthetic or anonymized metadata.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP rules on OpenMetadata export paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files and app context, while OpenMetadata can operate through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap on the host, but they can both act on shared mutable resources through integrations, creating coordination risk. Because no locking or shared-state mechanism is documented, uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external catalog or API resource, concurrent updates can conflict.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks trigger actions while ChatGPT is editing related artifacts, stale writes become possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each resource.
Pause OpenMetadata automations during ChatGPT-assisted edits.
Use read-only access for ChatGPT when inspecting catalog state.
Add manual approval before any API write from either side.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata is a data-catalog and governance system, so its outputs are likely to be treated as authoritative context. ChatGPT Desktop can then summarize or transform that context, and downstream users may act on it without verification. The pairwise cascade is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata-derived facts are pasted into ChatGPT and then reused without verification, errors can propagate.
IF ChatGPT-generated summaries are used as governance inputs, downstream decisions may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Require source links in any ChatGPT summary of OpenMetadata data.
Verify critical fields against OpenMetadata before acting.
Mark ChatGPT outputs as draft-only for governance use.
Use a second reviewer for any decision based on the pair.
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving export from OpenMetadata to ChatGPT.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata is open-source and primarily a governance/catalog tool, while ChatGPT Desktop is a vendor-managed service that processes uploaded files and app context. The main compliance issue is policy mismatch when regulated metadata is moved into ChatGPT; no specific residency or certification conflict is documented in the profiles, so the risk is limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated metadata from OpenMetadata is uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop, retention and residency policies may diverge.
IF the organization requires local-only handling for governance data, ChatGPT Desktop use would violate that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated metadata out of ChatGPT.
Use anonymized exports for analysis.
Confirm internal policy before sharing catalog data.
Log every transfer of governance data to ChatGPT.
requires-engineering: route regulated workflows to a compliant local toolchain.
